neighbours.label: 'how' (in 'how many') and 'number' (in 'the number of') when asking for a count
fire: Tom has 12 apples and gives 5 to his sister. How many apples does he have left?
A bus carries 40 people and 15 get off at the first stop. How many remain on board?
Count the dots on each card and write the number of dots in the box.
There are 8 red marbles and 3 more blue marbles than red. How many blue marbles are there?
Look at each insect and circle the number of legs it has.
The survey asks each school how many teachers it employs this year.
If a class has 30 pupils and 18 are boys, how many girls are in the class?
Use the table to find the number of students who walk to school.
quiet: Tom has 12 apples and gives 5 to his sister, who eats them at lunch.
A bus carries 40 people and 15 get off at the first stop near the park.
Look at the dots on each card and colour the card you like best.
There are 8 red marbles and some blue marbles in the glass jar on the desk.
Look at each insect and colour its wings with a bright crayon.
The survey asks each school whether its teachers enjoy their work.
A class has 30 pupils, and the boys and girls sit at long tables.
Use the table to see which students walk to school on Mondays.

notes: card: ' number' x9, ' how'/' How' x13 in counting word problems; the + pole is 'few in number', so the axis is about counts
